title: QBR Token Exposure Scenarios & Alert Playbook
content:
Purpose
This worksheet is a practical QBR artifact for CS managers and renewal teams to review token exposure, identify rate-limit risk, and propose budget alerting/actions ahead of renewal conversations. It is intentionally lightweight and scenario-driven so it can be dropped into a QBR deck or used as a meeting guide.

How to use this doc (quick):
- Pre-QBR: pull last 90 days of token usage by API route + model. Populate the "Recent usage snapshot" section.
- During QBR: step through the three scenario blocks (steady growth, burst event, accidental leak) and confirm recommended mitigations.
- Post-QBR: assign owners for alerts, throttles, and CS action items in the Action table.

Executive summary (one-line):
Customer currently has medium token exposure with two high-burn routes (chat/completion) and one occasional burst pattern. If current growth continues, expected monthly spend will exceed reserved budget in 7 weeks. Recommend enabling budget alerting, adding route-level quotas, and scheduling an engineering deep-dive on caching/batch strategy.

Recent usage snapshot (last 90 days) — required fields to fetch before QBR:
- Total tokens consumed (90d): [PLACEHOLDER]
- Tokens by model (top 5): e.g., redwood-2-large: 42%, open-llama-3: 24%, tiny-embed: 12%
- Tokens by endpoint/route (top 5): chat-api (48%), embeddings-bulk (18%), search-rerank (12%), docs-summarize (9%), test-playground (5%)
- 95th percentile request size (tokens): [PLACEHOLDER]
- Peak sustained qps for tokenized routes (last 30d): [PLACEHOLDER]
- Rate-limit incidents in 90d: count and brief notes (route, date, duration)

Key signals to spot pre-QBR (automate these checks in the CS dashboard):
- Sudden move in median request size > 2x week-over-week
- More than 3% of requests hitting model-level soft limits
- New client-side codepaths with >10k tokens/request in dev logs
- Sustained SST (sustained spike threshold) over 5 minutes at >3x baseline qps

Three risk scenarios (fill numbers during prep):
1) Steady growth scenario\- Input: baseline monthly tokens *growth rate* (e.g., 15% MoM)\- Impact: project token spend for next 12 weeks, compute runway to next budget commit\- Triage/playbook: if projected spend > 90% of committed budget within 8 weeks -> run canary to reduce default temperature/prompt length for top 3 routes; enable cost tags and daily usage digest to stakeholders
2) Burst event (legit traffic spike)\- Input: observed historical peak * multiplier (e.g., 2x, 5x)\- Impact: risk of hitting cluster limits and causing 429s or failover to cheaper model variants\- Triage/playbook: implement temporary route-level rate limiting at client tier; enable auto-fallback to cheaper compatible model variant; notify SRE/Platform via Slack channel and open an incident playbook
3) Accidental leak / test runaway\- Input: single-client continuous high-rate calls with large contexts (e.g., >50k tokens/day from one API key)\- Impact: immediate budget exhaustion and potential throttles during renewals discussion\- Triage/playbook: rotate the key, add per-key daily caps, disable anonymous test tokens, open a CS ticket with customer to review testing practices

Sample alert thresholds and suggested actions (tunable per account):
- Daily spend alert: 70% of daily budget -> notify CS owner + customer billing contact (Slack + email)
- Runner alert: 90% of monthly committed budget -> page CS lead and finance analyst (pager or high-urgency Slack)
- Burst detection: more than 10% of daily tokens consumed in a 15-min window -> auto-create incident in ops queue + Slack alert to #cs-usage-alerts
- Per-route 95th-percentile tokens threshold breach -> create task for eng to evaluate batching/caching opportunities

Sample budget math cheatsheet (copyable)
- Cost per 1k tokens = $X (fill from pricing)
- Daily budget = committed_monthly_budget / 30
- Tokens remaining in month = (committed_budget - spent_so_far) / cost_per_1k_tokens * 1000
- Runway weeks = tokens_remaining / average_weekly_token_burn

Quick SQL/BI snippets (BigQuery style) to populate dashboard metrics\- daily_token_burn_by_key:
SELECT date, api_key, SUM(input_tokens + output_tokens) AS tokens
FROM `redwood_prod.logs.tokens`
WHERE date BETWEEN DATE_SUB(CURRENT_DATE(), INTERVAL 90 DAY) AND CURRENT_DATE()
GROUP BY date, api_key
ORDER BY date DESC

- top_routes_last_30d:
SELECT route, SUM(tokens) as tokens FROM `redwood_prod.logs.tokens`
WHERE date >= DATE_SUB(CURRENT_DATE(), INTERVAL 30 DAY)
GROUP BY route ORDER BY tokens DESC LIMIT 10

Escalation playbook (roles + timing)
- CS owner: 0–4 hours (initial message to customer, context capture)
- SRE/platform on-call: 1–2 hours (confirm whether 429s are infra vs user-driven)
- Finance: 24 hours (confirm billing exposure and whether credit/commit adjustments needed)
- Product/Eng: 72 hours (if rate-limits or model fallbacks need code changes)

Rate limit configuration suggestions (practical knobs)
- Per-key daily token cap (soft): start at 1.5x past-30d average to avoid false positives\- Route-level concurrency cap: 50 concurrent requests for chat endpoints for mid-tier customers\- Burst window token cap: 15-min sliding window equal to 1.5x historical peak

Mitigation playbook (operational actions CS can run quickly)
- Immediate (within meeting): enable email + Slack alerting for 70% daily spend; temporarily increase debounce on client retries to reduce accidental amplification\- Short-term (1–7 days): assign eng to add route-level fallback to cheaper model; add caching layer for repeated prefixes; request customer to enable client-side rate limiting\- Medium-term (2–6 weeks): add autoscaling policies or reserved capacity options; review prompt engineering to reduce context sizes and avoid long system messages

Customer-facing scripts (copy-paste friendly)
- High spend notification template: "Hi <NAME>, we're seeing your account consuming tokens at a rate that could exceed your monthly budget within X days. We've temporarily enabled an alert and recommend scheduling a short call to review throttles and fallback models. Suggested time slots: ..."
- Burst follow-up update: "Incident summary: spike observed on <ROUTE> at <TIME>, root cause suspected to be <CAUSE>, action taken: <ACTION>. Next steps: <ACTIONS>"

Action table (fill during QBR):
- Action: Enable 70% daily spend alert -> Owner: Aisha Patel -> Due: 2026-02-21 -> Status: TODO
- Action: Add per-key daily cap for API keys listed -> Owner: Engineering CS -> Due: 2026-03-01 -> Status: TODO
- Action: Schedule prompt optimization session with customer -> Owner: Jonah Reed -> Due: 2026-02-28 -> Status: TODO

Appendix: recommended view to add to the QBR deck
- Slide 1: 90d token trend + 30/60/90 day moving averages
- Slide 2: Top 5 token-consuming routes + average token/request
- Slide 3: Scenario outputs (steady growth / burst / leak) with projected spend and recommended actions
- Slide 4: Current alerting and handoff matrix (who we call at each threshold)

Notes & known limitations
- This worksheet assumes token pricing and contract terms are available — fill cost per token before running math.
- Does not replace a full security incident response; for suspected abuse/leak contact security immediately.
- Some remediation (e.g., fallback models) requires product/infra coordination and cannot be toggled instantly for every account.

Open questions (for internal prep)
- Do we have automations to create per-account PagerDuty escalations, or is Slack sufficient?
- Can Finance enable temporary commit top-ups for accounts mid-cycle without contract changes?
- Are there pre-approved fallback model variants per customer tier? (prod -> cheaper fallback list)

Revision history
- 2025-11-03: initial draft (Aisha Patel)
- 2025-12-07: added SQL snippets and escalation timing (Jonah Reed)
- 2026-02-14: tuned alert thresholds and appended QBR slide guidance (Sofia Nguyen)
